name: @effectified/maplibre-gl
tagline: a WebGL map whose camera is the Model

decisions.question: Which exported functions and classes does the facade offer?
decisions.why: the README's example starts from `new maplibregl.Map({ container, style, center, zoom })`; markers, popups and controls attach to a map. In the frontend facade the Map is held by the `Map` mount, not wrapped as an export

decisions.question: Which method releases a Map$1, so acquiring one opens a scope? ("none" keeps it unscoped)
decisions.why: Map.remove() is MapLibre's teardown ("Clean up and release all internal resources associated with this map"): its DOM elements, event bindings, web workers and WebGL resources. `stop` only stops a camera animation; the drafter picked it because `remove` is not among its release names

Which upstream failures become which tagged errors?
decisions.answer: AJAXError <- instanceof AJAXError; GPUInitializationError <- instanceof GPUInitializationError; MaplibreGlError
decisions.why: exported error classes, most specific first, then the catch-all MaplibreGlError carrying `code` (the source sets no codes)

decisions.question: Which handles are provided as services (Context.Service with a layer)?
decisions.why: every offered export that acquires a releasable handle

decisions.question: Which mounts does the frontend facade offer?
decisions.why: a map lives on one <div>: created from its style, center and zoom (upstream's StyleSpecification | string and LngLatLike), updated in place (setStyle only when the style changed, jumpTo only when the camera changed and is not the map's own camera echoed back by the Model, so a gesture is not interrupted), its moveend camera and clicks as plain [lng, lat] data, removed with map.remove()

decisions.question: Which release of its upstream's major.minor is the facade? (its npm version is `<major>.<minor>.<revision - 1>`)
decisions.why: engine 0.5.0: published on npm as 6.19.4 (`npm install @effectified/maplibre-gl effect`), its version maplibre-gl's major.minor and the facade's releases for it (4 before this one, GitHub releases `maplibre-gl-v6.19.0` to `maplibre-gl-v6.19.0+4`); its package.json names effectified/packages as its repository, which npm checks as the release workflow publishes, and its README, skill and docs.json install it from npm by name
